text.en:
Every morning Kamala akka swept the school before anyone came. One day the floor was spotless for the annual day.
The headmaster thanked her in front of everyone. "Without her work our school could not run," he said.
The children clapped loudly.

Every honest work is valuable, whether it is done by a doctor, a farmer, a cleaner or a cobbler. Respecting all work is called dignity of labour.
Work is done for earning, for the family and for the community. People who work with their hands give us food, houses, clean streets and clothes.
We should thank workers, not look down on them. Gandhiji too did his own work such as spinning and cleaning, to show that no work is small.
Every honest work is valuable. Respecting all work is dignity of labour.
Farmers, cleaners, tailors and doctors all help society.
We should thank workers and not look down on them.
Gandhiji did his own work to show that no work is small.

problem.en: Is a cleaner's work less important than a teacher's?

text.en: A cleaner keeps the school healthy and safe.
Both are important, so we must respect both equally.

prompt.en: A friend laughs at a classmate whose father is a cobbler. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: Making and repairing shoes is honest and useful work.

points.en: Dignity of labour means respecting all work.
We should thank those whose work helps us.
